_comment: Alaska GOAL Program Rating and Award Criteria Plan (Qualified Allocation Plan), AHFC, version June 24, 2026. One plan rates applications for LIHTC, HOME, SCHDF and NHTF together. The document states no cycle year; the FY2027 in the filename is not on its face, so the cycle is left to data/sources.csv. Page numbers are PDF page indices and match the printed 'Page N of 51'. Rating criteria pp.21-36, with a RATING AND RANKING CRITERIA SUMMARY on pp.38-39 stating each section maximum and 'TOTAL POINTS 231'. The summary and the body agree on every section maximum and every item value. Hand-summed before loading: 21 + 52 + 38 + 45 + 40 + 28 + 1 + 6 = 231. One section needed a cap to reach it: Section 3 Project Characteristics states a maximum of 38 and its nine items sum to 46. The difference is exactly the 8-point Senior Housing Offset, and the plan states no rule excluding it from anything; recorded as a capped_sum group at 38 with the reasoning in the 3.h note. Two drafting errors are recorded: 5.a.iv cross-refers to '3(a)(iii)' where it means its own item, and the 4.a unemployment ladder's fifth tier reads 'at least equal to the statewide rate'. Thresholds are in AK_thresholds.json.

track_totals.note: RATING AND RANKING CRITERIA SUMMARY, pp.38-39: 'TOTAL POINTS 231', the sum of eight section maxima (21, 52, 38, 45, 40, 28, 1, 6). Section 3's items sum to 46 against its stated 38; the capped_sum group at 38 is what makes the computed total match. Penalty points have no maximum and are excluded, as are the 5.a.v and 5.b.iii deductions. The summary marks Underwriting as carrying an '8 point threshold': an application must earn at least 8 of its 40 points to be funded.

groups.label: Project Characteristics, capped at 38
groups.note: Nine items sum to 46 (12 + 1 + 8 + 12 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 8 + 2) against the stated section maximum of 38, both in the body on p.25 and in the summary on p.38. The gap equals the Senior Housing Offset; see the 3.h note.

criteria.heading: Small community
criteria.quote: Project is located in an area qualifying as a “small community,” as defined in this
criteria.note: The largest single fixed award in the plan. A small community is one of 6,500 or fewer people not connected by road or rail to Anchorage or Fairbanks, or of 1,600 or fewer that is connected and at least 50 miles from Anchorage or 25 from Fairbanks (definition, p.8). The Alaska Marine Highway does not count as a road connection.

criteria.heading: QCT contributing to a community revitalization plan
criteria.quote: and is considered to contribute to a community revitalization plan
criteria.note: One point, against 20 for a small community: the plan weights rural remoteness far above the federal QCT/revitalization preference.

criteria.heading: Energy efficiency
criteria.quote: Energy Efficiency (14 Points)

tiers.tier_label: 5 Star Plus and BEES, moderate cost area
5 Star Plus and BEES, intermediate cost area
5 Star Plus and BEES, high-cost area
Cost effective building improvements, rehab only, at least $40 per unit per year
Cost effective renewable energy, at least $40 per unit per year
Cost effective energy efficiency improvements beyond 5 Star Plus BEES, at least $40 per unit per year

criteria.note: Two either/or families: (i)-(iv) are alternatives ('Points may be awarded under only one category'), worth at most 8; (v) and (vi) are alternatives ('Applicants may receive points for one category, but not both'), worth 6. 8 + 6 = the stated 14. The 5 Star Plus award depends on the cost area the site sits in, not on the building. Cost effectiveness is a payback test over the lesser of 30 years or system life with energy prices escalated at 3%. Recipients must supply annual financial statements and answer energy consumption inquiries for the term of the covenants.

criteria.heading: Availability of larger units for households with children
criteria.quote: Availability of Larger Units for Households with Children (Maximum 2 Points)
criteria.note: Points = (units with 3+ bedrooms x 2) / (total residential units x 0.4), so full points at 40% of units. The worked example gives 0.5 points, so fractional points are awarded.

criteria.heading: Units equipped for persons with physical disabilities and sensory impairments
criteria.quote: Number of Units Equipped for Persons with Physical Disabilities and Sensory
criteria.note: Senior: equipped units x 8 / total units, so full points only at 100% equipped. Non-senior: equipped units x 8 / (total units x 0.25), full points at 25%. The threshold already requires 5% equipped for physical disabilities and 2% for sensory impairments in projects of 5 or more units; the formula as written does not net those out.

criteria.heading: Rehabilitation project
criteria.quote: Rehabilitation Project (Maximum 16 points)

tiers.tier_label: Any project involving rehabilitation, including demolition within 3 years
Area with negative three-year average population growth
Area with vacancy above the statewide average
Converts a non-affordable property to affordable, or non-senior to senior

criteria.note: 2 + 4 + 4 + 6 = the stated 16. The last three require meeting the minimum rehabilitation cost in the Project Cost and Funding Limitations section. Two of them reward weak markets (shrinking population, high vacancy) using the same data that Section 4 uses to reward strong ones, so a rehab project's Market Conditions and Rehabilitation scores pull against each other.

criteria.heading: Storage facilities
criteria.quote: All residential units will be provided with assigned tenant
criteria.note: Units with attached garages qualify automatically.

criteria.heading: Service enriched housing
criteria.quote: Service enriched housing, which incorporates substantive social services for
criteria.note: Only where homeless or disabled households are served through hard set-aside units, with service costs and funding in the operating budget.

criteria.heading: Project based rental assistance
criteria.quote: Project Based Rental Assistance (8 points)
criteria.note: Federal project-based assistance on at least 25% of units for at least 15 years. GOAL rental subsidy sources do not qualify.

criteria.heading: Project serves the lowest income tenants
criteria.quote: Project Serves the Lowest Income Tenants (Maximum 12 Points)
criteria.note: ((50% AMI units - 10% of units) x 12) / (50% of units), floored at 0 and capped at 12, so points start above 10% of units and max out at 60%. Worked example on p.26: 50 of 97 units gives 9.97. Senior projects requesting only SCHDF funds are rated excluding this criterion.

criteria.heading: Extended low-income project use
criteria.quote: One (1) point will be awarded to applications that commit the project to an
criteria.note: 30 years of extended use, and LIHTC sponsors taking the point forfeit the qualified contract route. SCHDF-only senior projects are rated excluding this criterion.

criteria.heading: Projects which serve special needs populations
criteria.quote: Projects which Serve Special Needs Populations (8 Points Maximum)
criteria.note: (Special needs units beyond the 5% threshold x 8) / (50% of units), so full points at an additional 50% of units. Special needs includes households at or below 30% AMI, except for SCHDF-only projects.

criteria.heading: Project mix
criteria.quote: Project Mix (12 Points Maximum)

tiers.tier_label: Tract with 51%+ of households above AMI: 65% low-income units
Tract with 40-51% of households above AMI: 65% low-income units
Tract with 20%+ of households below 30% AMI: 20% of units at or above market rate
Project mix bonus, any tract: at least 20% unrestricted with the rest restricted, or the reverse

criteria.note: Three tract-dependent ladders and a bonus. The two affluent-tract ladders are exclusive by definition, since a tract cannot be both above and below 51%; whether a tract could qualify for (i) or (ii) and (iii) at once is not addressed. The best ladder pays 8 and the bonus 4, which makes the stated 12. The ladders pull opposite ways: in affluent tracts more low-income units score higher, in poor tracts more market-rate units do. Census tract eligibility is set at pre-application from a required market study.

criteria.heading: Projects intended for eventual tenant ownership
criteria.quote: Projects Intended for Eventual Tenant Ownership (1 Point)
criteria.note: Requires a homeownership counseling plan and resale restrictions.

criteria.heading: Preference in occupancy for homeless families
criteria.quote: Preference in Occupancy for Homeless Families (1 Point)

criteria.heading: Public housing waiting lists
criteria.quote: Public Housing Waiting Lists (1 Point)
criteria.note: Requires rents below the AHFC Payment Standard (or HUD FMR) and a referral relationship with AHFC or an Indian Housing Authority; no point where no such office can provide referrals.

criteria.heading: Senior housing offset
criteria.quote: Senior Housing Offset (8 Points)
criteria.note: Eight points for projects primarily housing senior households, but none if income-restricted funding encumbers more than 20% of the units. This is the item that accounts for the Section 3 gap: the nine items sum to 46 and the section maximum is 38, a difference of exactly 8. The plan states no rule making the offset exclusive of anything. Its 20% restriction ceiling does limit 3.a in practice: a project with at most 20% restricted units can score at most 2.4 there. That looks like the intent of the name, compensating senior projects that cannot earn the income-targeting points, but it is an inference. Coded inside a capped_sum group at 38 rather than as an exclusivity rule nobody wrote. Reviewer should confirm.

criteria.heading: Veterans housing preference
criteria.quote: Veterans Housing Preference (2 Points)

criteria.heading: Opportunity (unemployment relative to statewide rate)
criteria.quote: Opportunity: (up to 15 Points)

tiers.tier_label: At least equal to the statewide rate

criteria.note: Borough or census area unemployment from the Department of Labor. The fifth tier reads 'at least equal to the statewide rate', which taken literally includes every rate above it; it presumably means equal to or below. Reviewer should read p.29. The whole section scores the strength of the local market, which works against the 20-point small community award for remote places.

criteria.heading: Rental market strength (vacancy)
criteria.quote: Rental Market Strength (up to 15 Points)
criteria.note: Department of Labor Rental Market Indicators survey, or a market study using the same method outside the survey areas.

criteria.heading: Location trends (population growth)
criteria.quote: Location Trends (up to 15 Points)

tiers.tier_label: Borough or census area under 6,500 people with growth above 0%

criteria.note: Communities under 6,500 are scored on the lesser of community and borough growth; Palmer and Wasilla are combined. A shrinking place below -0.5% scores nothing, though the same decline earns 4 points under 2.d.ii for a rehab project.

criteria.heading: Pro forma analysis
criteria.quote: Pro Forma Analysis (30 Points)

tiers.tier_label: Automatic, projects barred from servicing debt (e.g. HUD 811, Section 202)
RDAW fee and contingency line items at or below limits
All RDAW line items clearly described (minus 2 per vague 'other' line)

criteria.note: The hard debt ladder and the 14-point automatic award are alternatives; the RDAW items are additive. 24 + 1 + 5 = the stated 30. Rewarding more hard debt is unusual. Remote small communities not on the road or rail system score the ladder at 40% of the target percentages, so 'more than 6%' earns 24 there. Item iv's deduction runs 'until points are no longer available under 3(a)(iii)', which is a cross-reference to Project Characteristics and cannot be right; it presumably means 5(a)(iv). Recorded as a drafting error.

criteria.heading: Penalty: RDAW discrepancy
criteria.quote: Penalty: RDAW Discrepancy (minus 5 points maximum).
criteria.note: One point per instance: omitted costs, sources or expenses not in the workbook, or sources and uses more than $1,000 apart.

criteria.heading: Developer fee
criteria.quote: Developer Fee (2 Points)

tiers.tier_label: Developer overhead and fee in excess of overhead in separate line items
No deferred developer fee at or above 30% of total fee

criteria.heading: Penalty: deferred fee not repayable within 12 years
criteria.quote: not repayable within 12 years based on trending analysis in the Rental
criteria.note: Applies only where the developer is not the project owner.

criteria.heading: Debt coverage ratio
criteria.quote: Debt Coverage Ratio   (8 Points)

tiers.tier_label: Year-one DCR at or above 1.40, hard debt at least 4% of TDC
Automatic, projects barred from servicing debt

criteria.note: Projects that cannot carry debt receive the full 8 automatically here, but only 14 of 24 in 5.a, so the offset is partial.

criteria.heading: Appropriateness of total development cost per unit
criteria.quote: The appropriateness of the project’s total development cost (TDC) per unit in the
criteria.note: Ranked by a review committee of at least three from a narrative of up to 6 pages; points are 'evenly distributed down the consolidated average ranking', with the top proposal getting the maximum. The score depends entirely on the other applications.

criteria.heading: GOAL funding relative to TDC and other funding
criteria.quote: The amount of GOAL funding requested relative to the TDC and the amount of
criteria.note: Committee-ranked as 6.a.

criteria.heading: Non-profit or regional housing authority participation
criteria.quote: A tax-exempt organization or Regional Housing Authority is involved in the project on
criteria.note: Involvement must be regular, continuous and substantial in both development and operation.

criteria.heading: Penalty points for past performance
criteria.quote: Points will be deducted from the applicant’s score in cases where a principal of the
criteria.note: No maximum ('Penalty points - no max' in the p.39 summary), so points_max is null. Four schedules: 1 point per late grant progress report after the first; 1 point per month an AHFC mortgage payment is 30 days late, capped at 5; 3 points per project with an uncorrected 8823, non-compliant review or audit finding; and for unapproved scope changes on a prior project, the greater of 3 points per instance or the points originally awarded for the broken commitment. Assessed at pre-application and curable up to 45 days before the full application deadline.

criteria.heading: Job training program
criteria.quote: Job Training Program (Maximum 6 Points)
criteria.note: One point per on-the-job trainee during development, plus 2 for classroom training of at least 20 hours for at least two of those trainees, capped at 6. Failing to run the program can lead AHFC to recapture the award.
